Write P_i = L(lambda_i) for their chronological target products. Define the guarded boundary condition G on a valid full configuration by:

1. Every one of the 177113 pieces outside K has exactly its sigma pose.
2. All seven K pieces share an exact pose Q = L(u) Qstar, where u is an exact unit quaternion and ||u-1|| <= 1/200.
3. The left height H is at least 3888 and the left-tree branch is 2.

The admitted language consists of finite concatenations of W_i starting at sigma for which every boundary satisfies G. The source's deterministic first-containing-box family is an unbounded subset. The present decoder does not require or certify that deterministic choice rule; it recognizes the larger admitted guarded language.

Check G using the full outside-K matrices and the common exact K pose. Reject on failure. Then perform the following exact procedure, storing the proposed inverse blocks rather than consulting an input history:

```
if the full state is exactly sigma:
    accept

if H <= 3888 but the state is not exactly sigma:
    reject

for i = 0,...,6:
    Qprev = P_i^-1 Q
    retain i only if Qprev satisfies the exact Euclidean guard,
    has branch 2, has height at least 3888, and lowers height

if the number retained is not exactly one:
    reject

replace Q by that predecessor and append W_i^-1 to the output
repeat
```

The outside background is the fixed sigma background at every proposed boundary. The tree-code result forces every retained transition to lower height by exactly 2|W_i|, not merely by a positive amount. Each iteration therefore lowers height by at least 132, so there are at most floor((H-3888)/132) iterations. A different pose at height 3888 is not an accepting terminal state.

For an admitted guarded concatenation, its actual last word supplies a candidate: its preceding boundary satisfies G. Prefix incomparability makes that candidate unique. Induction strips the whole concatenation and reaches exact sigma. This proves completeness on the stated language.

Conversely, if the decoder reaches sigma, read its proposed predecessor chain forward. At each guarded boundary, the published isolation and perturbation results make the corresponding W_i admissible, return all outside-K poses, and give precisely P_i Qprev as the next common K pose. Starting from the genuine sigma state, this reconstructs the accepted input as an admitted concatenation. Reversing this legal chain proves that the emitted inverse word is legal. This proves sound recognition and the full collateral-effect assertion.

For an accepted input of height H, decoding to sigma uses

```
sum_i |W_i| = (H-3888)/2
```

letters. Appending that fixed history suffix produces a state-only return word of length

```
(H-3888)/2 + 1824 = (H-240)/2.
```

Every literal letter of the emitted word lowers the height of each K piece by exactly 2: this follows from the source's strict forward pump property for inverse blocks, and from saturation of the height bound for the fixed suffix.

Now fix any one of the seven labelled K pieces. Every legal I_a menu letter, at any grip, changes its height by at most 2. Hence any competing path from the accepted input to a state where that piece has height at most 240 has length at least (H-240)/2. The constructed word attains the bound.

Thus the exact full-state distance to the fixed tau240 endpoint is (H-240)/2. The same number is the minimum reach distance if any one, or all seven, of these K pieces must reach height at most 240. Adding exact outside-K endpoint restoration leaves these minima unchanged because tau240 meets it. This does not claim equality for every individual target state with low height.

These are endpoint restoration statements. Other pieces may move during individual letters. The result does not cover arbitrary guarded-looking states that the decoder rejects, intermediate pump prefixes, split-K inputs, arbitrary reachable states, or lattice landing. The fixed seed suffix is a constant witness; no history of the input state is needed.

Let A be the guarded boundary language recognized by that document. Let V(i,k) be the first k letters of certificate word W_i, with 0 <= k < |W_i|. Define

    A_prefix = { V(i,k)(Y) : Y in A, i in {0,...,6}, 0 <= k < |W_i| }.

All these prefixes are legal at every Y in A. The source perturbation bounds were checked for every prefix of every W_i uniformly over the input ball, independently of the box chosen by the deterministic family rule. The full block might leave the guard if it was not the selected block; legality and strict height growth of its prefixes do not require the output guard.

The source step lemma gives h_K(V(i,k)(Y)) = h_K(Y) + 2k, and every K piece still shares a pose. The outside-K configuration depends only on the two cumulative finite debris labels of V(i,k), because every Y in A has the same sigma background. The finite prefix catalogue has 1746 occurrences before deduplication.

## Recognition without a recorded input history

For an input state S:

1. Require the seven labelled K pieces to share an exact pose Q.
2. For each catalogue entry (i,k), compare every outside-K canonical pose matrix with its exact prefix-background template. A pair of inferred debris labels can index candidates, but cannot replace this full comparison.
3. Let P(i,k) be the chronological target matrix product of the prefix. Form the boundary candidate with K pose P(i,k)^-1 Q and exact sigma background.
4. Run the guarded boundary recognizer on that candidate. On acceptance, also check h_K(S) - h_K(candidate) = 2k.
5. Return the literal inverse prefix, then the boundary decoder word, then the fixed sigma-to-tau240 suffix. If no candidate accepts, reject.

The finite enumeration may have several accepting descriptions. Uniqueness of a prefix description is neither required nor claimed. Any accepted description gives the same optimal total length.

For soundness, a recognized boundary candidate Y belongs to A. The source uniform prefix result makes V(i,k) legal at Y. Its target matrix and complete outside-K template reproduce S exactly. Therefore the literal inverse prefix is legal from S back to Y, with full collateral effects. Appending the already proved boundary return is legal and finishes at the same fixed tau240 state.

For completeness, an input in A_prefix has at least its defining (i,k,Y) description. The corresponding template matches, and the boundary recognizer accepts Y. No original input history is consulted.

Termination follows from the finite catalogue and the terminating boundary recognizer. A conservative number of boundary-decoder iterations per catalogue entry is floor((H-3888)/132), where H is the input K height. This is an iteration bound, not a claim about bit complexity of exact arithmetic.

## Exact depth

For any accepted description, the output length is

    k + (H - 2k - 240)/2 = (H - 240)/2.

Every legal I_a letter changes an individual piece's left height by at most 2. Hence no competing path to the fixed tau240 state, or to any state where a chosen one of these K pieces has height at most 240, can be shorter. The result also holds for the minimum to any or all seven K pieces at height at most 240, with optional exact equality to the sigma outside-K background at the endpoint. An intermediate input can have a different outside-K background; equality to that input background is not asserted.

Thus the earlier optimal state-only decoder extends from guarded block boundaries to every literal intermediate state of every admitted guarded concatenation. It also recognizes the extra safe prefixes in A_prefix as defined above. It does not cover arbitrary same-height states, arbitrary states passing only the Euclidean guard, or general lattice landing.

## Verification boundary

The proof is a finite-union closure consequence of the independently checked boundary theorem and the published uniform prefix admissibility result. The completed prototype is recorded in evidence/prefix-complete-optimal-decoder.json: 1746 occurrences give 1348 distinct exact product/background entries and 298 background-label pairs. Two intermediate inputs passed recognition and 620 total forward/inverse full-state replay letters; outside corruption and a guarded non-sigma floor state were rejected. The root independently recomputed all prefix products and labels, all seven complete tree-code vertices, and all21 pair distances in evidence/prefix-catalogue-independent-verified.json. PREFIX_COMPLETE_OPTIMAL_RETURN_REVIEW.md reviews the theorem and the explicit sigma-background endpoint contract. These checks establish the stated finite obligations and samples; the infinite claim still uses the written induction and published geometric premises.

Let S belong to the prefix-complete recognized language in PREFIX_COMPLETE_OPTIMAL_RETURN.md, and let H be the common left height of its seven labelled K pieces. The state-only prefix/boundary decoder returns from S to exact sigma in (H-3888)/2 letters.

Combining this with independently replayed finite suffixes gives:

| Fixed target configuration | K height | Rigorous distance interval from S |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| tau240, exact sigma background | 240 | exactly (H-240)/2 |
| tau28, exact sigma background | 28 | [(H-28)/2 + 1, (H-28)/2 + 2] |
| tau16, exact sigma background | 16 | [(H-16)/2, (H-16)/2 + 24] |
| Fully solved configuration | 0 | [H/2, H/2 + 68] |

The upper endpoints come respectively from suffix lengths 1824, 1932, 1960, and 2012 from sigma. The solved suffix is the literal inverse of the verified2012-letter solved-to-sigma witness: the original156-letter seed was compressed first to101 by locality rewrites, then to86 and83 by exact state-specific window substitutions, followed by the unchanged1929-letter pump. Independent join checks and full seed/inverse replays support the final83 seed (evidence/seed-state-local-shortening-review.json and evidence/seed-single-turn-window-shortening.json). The original gap141, locality-only gap86, and intermediate gap71 are superseded by68. The height part of every lower endpoint follows from the individual-piece 2-per-letter bound; tau28 additionally uses the first-step obstruction below. All lower endpoints apply against every alternative legal path using all600 grips. The intervals do not assert that the upper endpoint is optimal unless the interval is a singleton.

The tau28 construction is a uniform one-letter additive approximation to the exact fixed-target distance on this infinite recognizable family. It is not a multiplicative approximation for arbitrary states. The inverse-path first-step obstruction at tau28 raises the lower endpoint by1: every legal first letter there is neutral or lowering on every K piece. The matching two-letter first-raising example does not establish the exact long distance; evidence/tau28-firststep-independent-verified.json verifies the narrower interval.

### M1-09: bounds and finiteness (proved, model review)

- **Height-bounded search.** A search that keeps the left height of every piece at most 2m is finite. It has at most S_m = (7,200·D_m)^177,120 states, with D_m = (4·16^m − 1)/3 domains, so a target reachable within the restriction has a word of length at most S_m − 1.
- **Starting heights are not enough.** A bound on the heights of the start state does not keep a restoring word inside such a restriction.
- **Uniform bounds.** A uniform bound on the restoration length, or on one clean step at every reachable state, exists if and only if R(I_a) is finite (Card 5 Q1.1, open).

The s61c certificate stays at left height 2, so for that state the search with m = 1 (S_1 = 151,200^177,120 states) also succeeds. That is a statement about one state.

### AU-01 and AU-06: the general algorithm M\* (proved, model review)

**Theorem M\*.** For every reachable I_a configuration, the following algorithm reads only the current state and ends with all 259,800 sticker labels solved:
1. While a piece is off the lattice, list the units and pick one, U.
   - Try a finite batch of heuristics (the driver step, the pure twist, transport words). Accept only an exactly replayed clean step.
   - If none succeeds, enumerate all I_a menu words in order of length. Replay each from the state, and take the first clean step for U with free set off(Z) \ U.
2. When no piece is off the lattice, run the lattice restorer with a spanning library, corrections last.

It takes at most as many clean steps as there are off pieces at the start. It needs no history, no bound on heights and no finiteness of the reachable set.

*Proof.*
1. **The fallback stops.** The inverse of any history from the solved state is a clean step for U (M1-01). Each length has finitely many words, and every test is exact. The history appears only in the proof, never in the algorithm.
2. **Each step makes progress.** By Lemma U the next off set lies inside off(Z) \ U, so the off count falls by at least one. Every state stays reachable.
3. **The lattice phase finishes.** At the lattice endpoint Y, ν(Y) lies in A_J because Y is reachable. The library spans A_J, so a correction C with ν(C) = −ν(Y) exists. With T = solved·C⁻¹, the retained cascade takes Y to T in sticker labels, and C finishes (Theorem R, section 8). **QED**

The theorem gives no bound on the length of a fallback word. Lengths are bounded only for the toolkit, under the checks of AU-03, and for the lattice phase (AU-05).

### T9-05: bounded starting heights (proved, model review)

- **A finite maximum.** For each m, the reachable states whose pieces all have left height at most 2m have a finite maximum distance b(m) to the lattice. There are at most S_m of them (M1-09), and each has a finite restoration. This holds even if R(I_a) is infinite.
- **Not an explicit bound.** It does not give b(m) ≤ S_m − 1: that would need restorations that stay within the height restriction, and M1-09 shows that starting heights do not ensure this. Nor does it give an algorithm, since no procedure is known that recognizes when all reachable states of the restriction have been found.
- **M1-09 in both directions.**
  - A uniform clean-step length C restores any state to the lattice in at most 177,120·C letters. Each letter changes a height by at most 2, so every reachable height is at most 354,240·C.
  - A finite R(I_a) gives a path to solved of at most |R(I_a)| − 1 letters, which is a clean step for any unit.

### Theorem D (integrator; reviewed)

Setting (menu I_a, simulator semantics of `research/jumbling/sim/state.py`):
- A pose is a rotation x ↦ l x r̄ with unit quaternions l and r, taken up to the common sign of (l, r). G0 is the set of poses with l in Λ (the icosians of reduced norm 1, with 2 inverted) and r in 2I; K⁺ (order 7,200) is the set of poses with l and r in 2I, the lattice poses. Every menu rotation lies in G0 and G0 is a group, so every reachable pose lies in G0.
- The universe is the set (G0)^N of pose tables, N = 177,120. It is decidable: recover (l, r) up to sign from a 4 × 4 matrix over Q(√5) (`trees.factors`), then check that l lies in the icosian ring with 2 inverted and has norm 1, and that r lies in 2I. Physical validity (disjoint pieces) is not part of the universe.
- A letter (x, j) is admissible at Z when it is a menu item and no piece straddles cut x (an exact test), and Z·(x, j) is its image. R ⊂ (G0)^N is the set of configurations reachable from solved. n(Z) is the number of pieces off the lattice (poses outside K⁺) and h(Z) the largest left height.
- A clean step at Z (the free form of M1-01) is a word w admissible from Z with off(Z·w) ⊆ off(Z) \ U for some unit U of Z, and β(Z) is the length of a shortest one. By M1-01, β(Z) is finite at every Z in R with n(Z) > 0.

Facts used:
- (F1) Exactness: admissibility, lattice membership, units and the clean-step condition are decided exactly and finitely from the pose table, at every Z in (G0)^N, reachable or not.
- (F2) Reversibility (M1-01, part 1): if (x, j) is admissible at Z, its inverse letter is admissible at Z·(x, j) and returns Z. Each menu rotation fixes the normal of its cut, so the moved set is the same; this holds at every configuration.
- (F3) Bounded height is finite and listable inside G0. Λ acts on the 5-regular tree with vertex stabilizer 2I and one orbit on the even vertices, so the poses of G0 with left height at most 2m number 7,200·D_m, D_m = (4·16^m − 1)/3 (M1-09). They are listed by forming the products of at most m menu rotations (one jumble reaches each of the 20 vertices at distance 2, and induction along two-edge segments reaches every even vertex within distance 2m), multiplying each on the right by every element of K⁺, and removing duplicates exactly. Without the restriction to G0 the statement is false: the rotations x ↦ q_t x with q_t = ((t² − 1)/(t² + 1), 2t/(t² + 1), 0, 0), t even, are infinitely many, and all have both tree heights 0 (review finding D-01).
- (F4) The lattice base case: L = (K⁺)^N is finite, so R ∩ L has a computable characteristic function, a finite table. This is an existence statement, and the table is not known. Theorem R does not supply it, because Theorem R restores sticker labels and allows hidden piece rotations, while R is defined by exact poses (review finding D-02).

**Theorem D.** The following are equivalent.
- (a) There is a computable B: ℕ × ℕ → ℕ with β(Z) ≤ B(n(Z), h(Z)) for every Z in R with n(Z) > 0.
- (b) There is a total computable F: (G0)^N → ℕ with β(Z) ≤ F(Z) for every Z in R with n(Z) > 0.
- (c) Membership in R is decidable on (G0)^N.
- (d) There is a computable H: ℕ → ℕ such that every Z in R is joined to solved by an admissible path along which every configuration has left heights at most H(h(Z)).
- (e) The complement (G0)^N \ R is recursively enumerable. (R itself is: enumerate the words from solved, by (F1).)

*Proof.*
- (a) ⇒ (b): F(Z) = B(n(Z), h(Z)); n and h are computable by (F1).
- (b) ⇒ (c): DECIDE(Z): if n(Z) = 0, look Z up in the table of (F4). Otherwise test every word of length at most F(Z) (F1). If none is a clean step, answer "not in R". Otherwise let w be the first, Z′ = Z·w, and answer DECIDE(Z′). The recursion ends, since n(Z′) < n(Z), and it stays in (G0)^N. If Z is in R, a clean step of length at most F(Z) exists and Z′ is in R, so by induction the answer is "in R". If Z is not in R, either no clean step is found (correct), or Z′ is not in R, because Z = Z′·w⁻¹ by (F2), and by induction the answer is "not in R". F need not bound anything at unreachable inputs (review finding D-03).
- (c) ⇒ (a): set B(0, h) = 0, and B(n, h) = 0 for n > N (review finding D-04). For 0 < n ≤ N, list by (F3) the finite set S(n, h) of tables in (G0)^N with n off pieces and left heights at most h; keep those in R (c); for each, find β by searching words in order of length (finite by M1-01); let B(n, h) be the largest (0 if none is kept).
- (c) ⇒ (d): for each h, list R_h = R ∩ {left heights ≤ h} as above. For each Z in R_h, run breadth-first searches from solved inside left heights ≤ m for m = h, h + 2, … until Z is found. Each search is finite by (F3), and one succeeds, since a path from solved to Z exists and has a largest height. H(h) is the largest m used.
- (d) ⇒ (c): run the breadth-first search from solved inside left heights ≤ H(h(Z)), a finite graph by (F3). By (F2) a path from Z to solved, reversed, is a path from solved to Z, so Z is in R exactly when it is found.
- (c) ⇔ (e): R is recursively enumerable, and a subset of a decidable universe is decidable exactly when it and its complement are recursively enumerable. ∎

(b) ⇒ (c) and (d) ⇒ (c) use the finite table of (F4) only for configurations with every piece on the lattice; with a constructive decision procedure for R ∩ L, every implication is constructive.

What it says (review finding D-05):
- An explicit bound for M1 in (n, h), or through any other total computable features of the state, gives a decision procedure for reachability; a decision procedure gives a bound in (n, h) and on full pose tables, though not on every prescribed set of features (constant features would demand the uniform bound that X1 rules out).
- The same problem in a third form is height confinement: how high must a restoring path climb above the state's own heights? A computable ceiling H(h) is equivalent to a bound.
- T9-05 and R21-08 give a finite maximum for each height; Theorem D says that turning it into a value is the same problem. It is a computability corollary of finite-search arguments. It gives neither a bound nor a decision, and it is not an impossibility result. A theorem of the form "every configuration with features (n, h) that satisfies checkable local conditions, which every reachable configuration satisfies, has a clean step of at most B letters" would prove (a).
- If strict steps exist at every reachable state with an off piece (Q2, open), the same proof with an exact test for strict steps gives the equivalence for strict steps.

**Proposition BN (bounded-excursion negatives) [Astra].** Fix an even E ≥ 0 and M = Φ(X) + E. A **negative certificate
with excursion E** at X is a finite set R of exact configurations containing X, each with Φ(X) ≤ Φ ≤ M, such that for
every member and every admissible letter whose result has Φ ≤ M, that result is in R. If one exists, no word from X with
excursion at most E lowers Φ. Conversely, if no such word exists, the set of configurations reached from X by words
whose prefixes all have Φ ≤ M is such a certificate, with at most [7200·(4·16^{q+1} − 1)/3]^177120 members, q = M/2.
A word of excursion E that lowers Φ together with a certificate with excursion E − 2 proves that E is the least
excursion.

*Proof.* Every prefix of a word with excursion at most E has Φ ≤ M, so by induction every prefix stays in R, where Φ is
at least Φ(X). Conversely, the set described is closed by construction, contains no configuration below Φ(X) (the word
reaching it would be a descent), and is finite: Φ ≤ M bounds every height by 2q + 2, and there are
(4·16^{q+1} − 1)/3 tree positions of height at most 2q + 2 (card 5), with 7200 poses each. Φ is even, so the least
excursion is even. ∎

Closure under neutral letters alone (stage 14, Proposition N) is not enough once E > 0: a word may raise, fall part of
the way and raise again. A certificate restricted to the letters of a declared family (the stop record of P*,
section 6) proves only that the family has no macro there. At the 7304 chain end the tame word R05 shows that no
certificate with excursion 0 exists, although the T3P scan is empty.

**Theorem GC (Good-set controller) [Astra].** Let x and z be clean at Z, with I_x ∩ I_z = G exactly, where G is a unit
(one pose) of height H ≥ 4; put B_x = I_x ∖ G and B_z = I_z ∖ G. Good_x is the set of items a at x such that every
piece of B_x at its pose times a is out at z; Good_z likewise. A controller state is (Q, a_x, a_z): the pose of G and
the products of the letters so far at x and at z. A letter (c, g), c ∈ {x, z}, is allowed when g·a_c ∈ Good_c, G at Q
is wholly in or wholly out at c, and G's height after the letter is at most H. Then every word of allowed letters is
admissible at Z; after it, B_x has its Z-poses times a_x, B_z times a_z, G has pose Q (updated only by the letters
whose cap holds it) and every other piece its Z-pose. Along such a word

    Φ ≤ Φ(Z) + 2(f_x + f_z),

where f_c is the number of pieces of B_c of height at least 2 and branch other than CLS(c) at Z. If at the end a_x and
a_z are retained and G has height at most H − 2, then Φ has fallen by at least 2|G|. The states are finite (at most
|Good_x||Good_z|·7200·(4·16^{H/2} − 1)/3), so if an accepting state can be reached, a word of at most that length
minus one reaches it.

*Proof.* This is the isolation lemma of X1 (stage 10, REPORT section 2.3) with the target G: before a letter at x, the
pieces of B_x are in cap x (a_x ∈ Λ_x keeps cap x), those of B_z are out at x (a_z ∈ Good_z), G is wholly in or out by
the rule, and every other piece has its Z-pose, at which it is neither in nor across x (I_x ∩ I_z = G and x is clean
at Z). So x is clean and the letter moves B_x and, when it holds G, G. The identity is in both Good sets, since B_x is
out at z at Z. For the bound: the change of φ over B_c is that of the single item a_c applied at Z (Lemma 5.2), which
raises only the f_c pieces, by 2 each (lattice pieces end at height 0 or 2, own-branch pieces keep or lose 2), and G
never exceeds H. With retained products the debris keep their heights, and G falls from H to at most H − 2. The count
of states: (4·16^{H/2} − 1)/3 tree positions of height at most H (card 5), 7200 poses each. ∎

**Proposition RP (reverse pump) [Claude Opus; return corrected by Astra].** In the setting of GC, let x have class Q,
z class P ≠ Q, and G branch Q and height H = 2m ≥ 4.
- (a) *Lowering phase.* A word of allowed letters that alternate between x and z, each in G's lowering coset at its
  grip and sending G into the class of the other grip, lowers G by 2 at each letter. After j letters
  Φ = Φ(Z) − 2|G|j + E_x(a_x) + E_z(a_z), where E_c(a) = Σ_{A∈B_c} [φ(aA) − φ(A)] ≤ 2f_c, and E_c(a) = 0 for a
  retained a.
- (b) *Return.* Let G end at height 2, let c be the grip that acted last on G and c′ the other. G has branch CLS(c′)
  and lies in cap c. A letter at c′ keeps G's height or lands it (a height-2 piece of branch CLS(c′)). If a_c is not
  retained, the return letter at c that makes its product retained is a jumble: if G is still in cap c, it raises G
  from 2 to 4, or from 0 to 2 if a letter at c′ has landed G. So, when a_c is not retained, both debris sets return to
  their heights with G at height at most 2 only if, before c's return, G has left cap c (by a landing letter at c′
  whose image of G is out at c, as in L9, or as in the lens cell LC1) or has been landed by a letter at c′ (it then
  ends at height 2, of branch CLS(c)). When a_c is retained, c has no return to make.
- (c) L9 (stage 14, section 6) is the case H = 4 with one lowering at x, a landing at z and a return at x only: I_x ∖ G
  returns exactly, and I_z ∖ G stays moved by g, with its Φ change at most 0 by the hypothesis F_z ≤ D_z(g).

The hypotheses are the GC tests at every letter, including the return letters: the exact pose and height of G must be
checked at each of them, since a return letter can move G and raise it again [Astra]. The length is at most the number
of lowering and landing letters plus two; the excursion is at most 2(f_x + f_z).

*Proof.* (a) GC and Lemma 5.2. (b) A letter at a grip maps its cap onto itself, so G is in cap c after c's last letter
on it. A jumble at a grip of class P raises by 2 every piece in its cap of height at least 2 and branch other than P,
and every lattice piece there, into branch P (Lemma 5.2); it keeps or lowers to 0 a height-2 piece of branch P. The
return item at c is r·a_c⁻¹ with r retained; A4_c is a subgroup, so it is retained exactly when a_c is. (c) is L9's
proof read in this setting. ∎

**Proposition V (whole pumps) [Astra; carry-over from X1 by both].** For a fixed pair x, z, a whole pump from a controller
state s exists exactly when s lies in the backward viability set of GC's controller restricted to the pump letters of
RP: V_0 the accepting states (both products retained, G at height at most 2, every return letter tested), and V_{j+1}
the states with an allowed pump letter into V_j. Membership is a finite exact computation, and a stored choice per state
constructs the word. Non-empty Good sets and three branch-compatible lowering items per rung do not imply membership.
From X1 the isolation lemma carries over; the step lemma's statement that every jumble raises K does not (a lowering
needs an item of the right coset), and neither do the X1 perturbation and covering lemmas, which control a pump that
raises K without bound.

*Proof.* The controller's states are finite and its transitions are tests at a state (GC); reachability of a finite set
in a finite graph is decided by the backward iteration. ∎

**Proposition P (termination) [both].** P* commits a macro only when Theorem MC certifies it at the current
configuration with Φ lower at its end and an excursion of at most E₀ (`macro.py` rejects every other candidate, of
every family, before it is committed). Then every run of P* ends after at most Φ(Z₀)/2 committed macros, and along the
whole executed word Φ ≤ Φ(Z₀) + E₀. A run that stops with Φ > 0 records, for each family, whether its search at the
stop was exhaustive; an exhaustive empty family is a negative certificate restricted to that family (Proposition BN
with the family's letters), not for all words.

*Proof.* Φ is a non-negative even integer, so each committed macro lowers it by at least 2; its excursion is at most E₀
above its own start, and its start is at most Φ(Z₀). ∎

Nothing here proves that P* reaches Φ = 0, or that it jams, at any configuration other than those it was run on
(README section 2.5).

### 2.2 Tree lemma (proved)
Let K be at left vertex z of height h ≥ 2 in branch β, and let (x, a) be a jumble at a grip x whose cap holds K,
where x has branch γ ≠ β. Then K moves to height h + 2 in branch γ.

*Proof.* The left part of every letter at x fixes w_x = n_x v0, and a jumble moves v0 (packet, section 2). The
geodesic from v0 to z starts with the edge v0 → w_β, and w_β ≠ w_x. Apply a. The path w_x, a·v0, a·w_β, …, a·z
has no backtracking, because a·w_β = w_x would give w_β = a⁻¹·w_x = w_x; so it is a geodesic of length h + 1.
Prefixing v0 → w_x gives a path without backtracking (a·v0 ≠ v0), hence a geodesic of length h + 2 that starts
towards w_x. ∎

### 2.3 Isolation lemma and step lemma (proved)
*Isolation lemma.* Let w = (x_1, a_1) … (x_m, a_m) be a word with every x_i in {c, d}. Let g_c^(i) and g_d^(i)
be the products, in order, of the letters at c, resp. d, among the first i. Let Q^(0) be K's pose at X, and
Q^(i) = E(x_i, a_i) Q^(i−1) if K at Q^(i−1) lies whole in cap x_i, else Q^(i) = Q^(i−1). Assume that for every
i, g_c^(i) is in Good_c, g_d^(i) is in Good_d, and K at Q^(i−1) lies whole in cap x_i or wholly outside its
interior. Then w is admissible from X. After i letters the pieces of D_c have their X-poses multiplied by
g_c^(i), those of D_d by g_d^(i), K has pose Q^(i), and all other pieces have their X-poses.

*Proof.* Induction on i; i = 0 is clear. Let letter i + 1 be (c, a); the case d is symmetric. A letter is
admissible exactly when its item is a menu item and no piece straddles its cut (`sim/state.py`, `apply`), and it
moves exactly the pieces whole in its cap. By the induction hypothesis:
- (i) a piece of D_c lies at g·(X-pose) with g in Λ_c; g fixes n_c, so the piece is still whole in cap c;
- (ii) a piece of D_d lies at g_d^(i)·(X-pose) with g_d^(i) in Good_d, so it lies out of cap c;
- (iii) K lies whole in cap c, or out of it, by assumption;
- (iv) any other piece has its X-pose. At X it was not whole in cap c (it is not in D_c ∪ K) and did not
  straddle cut c (I1), so it lies out of cap c. A piece of D_d is not whole in cap c, by (I2).

So nothing straddles cut c. The letter moves exactly D_c and, if K lies whole in cap c, K, and the poses become
the stated ones, since a·g_c^(i) = g_c^(i+1). ∎

*Kind and step.* A configuration is of kind S(h, x), x in {c, d}, if for some g_c in Good_c and g_d in Good_d:
- the pieces of D_c and D_d have their X-poses multiplied by g_c, resp. g_d, and the other pieces outside K
  have their X-poses;
- K lies whole in caps c and d at one pose of left height h ≥ 2, in the branch of the grip other than x.

*Step lemma.* Let Y be of kind S(h, x), y the other grip, and (x, a) a letter with a a jumble, a·g_x in Good_x,
and K, turned by a, whole in cap y. Then (x, a) is admissible at Y and the result is of kind S(h + 2, y).

*Proof.* Points (i)–(iv) of the proof of the isolation lemma, applied at Y with g_c^(i) = g_c and g_d^(i) = g_d,
use only the description of Y in S(h, x), together with (I1) and (I2). They show that no piece straddles cut x,
so (x, a) is admissible. They also show that it moves exactly D_x and K. Afterwards D_x is at
(a·g_x)·(X-pose) with a·g_x in Good_x, and the other pieces outside K are unchanged. K is whole in cap y by
hypothesis, and still whole in cap x because a fixes n_x. By the tree lemma (K is in the branch of y, and x
has the other branch) K's height is h + 2, in the branch of x. ∎

Grips other than c and d keep the products they have at X. So at most 18 + 2 = 20 grips are out at every state
of this kind: the out grips stay bounded, answering the owner's question of 17 October.

### 2.5 Perturbation lemma (proved)
Let W be a word with partial products P_k (P_0 = I), Q a pose of K, and η in (0, 1). Assume (*) holds for
m = n·(P_k Q v) − κ, for every k, every vertex v of K and both caps n. Then for every unit quaternion u with
|u − 1| ≤ η, and every k, K at pose P_k L(u) Q lies whole in caps c and d, and all its margins are > 0.

*Proof.* Fix k, v and n, and put w = Q v and n' = P_kᵀ n. Then n·(P_k L(u) Q v) = ⟨u w, n'⟩ = ⟨u, n' w̄⟩, by
⟨xy, z⟩ = ⟨x, z ȳ⟩ for quaternions. Let G = n' w̄. Then |G| = |n'| |w| = |n| |v|, because P_k and Q are
orthogonal. Also G_0 = ⟨1, n' w̄⟩ = ⟨w, n'⟩ = n·(P_k Q v) = m + κ. Here m > 0: the right side of (*) is ≥ 0,
so m > (m + κ)η²/2, which gives m(1 − η²/2) > κη²/2 > 0 (κ > 0, η < 1). Hence G_0 > 0. The square root is
real because m + κ = n·(P_k Q v) ≤ |n||v|. From |u − 1| ≤ η:
|u − 1|² = 2 − 2u_0, so u_0 ≥ 1 − η²/2 ≥ 0, and |u_vec|² = 1 − u_0² ≤ η². Hence
⟨u, G⟩ = u_0 G_0 + u_vec·G_vec ≥ (1 − η²/2)(m + κ) − η sqrt(|n|²|v|² − (m + κ)²). So
n·(P_k L(u) Q v) − κ ≥ m − (m + κ)η²/2 − η sqrt(|n|²|v|² − (m + κ)²) > 0. ∎

### 2.6 Covering lemma (proved from computation C)
For every unit quaternion u with |u − 1| ≤ η, some listed box b contains the vector part of u, and the word i of
any such box satisfies |λ_i u − 1| ≤ η.

*Proof.* u_0 ≥ 1 − η²/2 > 0, and |u_vec|² = 1 − u_0² ≤ R² := η² − η⁴/4 ≤ η². So u_vec lies in
[−η, η]³ ∩ {|x|² ≤ R²}. Computation C (`CERT.py`) subdivides [−η, η]³ into closed dyadic boxes, discarding a box
only when the minimum of |x|² on it exceeds R². It checks that every remaining leaf is a listed box (113 boxes,
16 split boxes), so the set is covered. For a listed box b with word i, C checks exactly that λ_{i,0} > 0 and
λ_{i,0} s_b − max_{x∈b} λ_{i,vec}·x ≥ 1 − η²/2, where s_b is a rational lower bound of
sqrt(1 − min(r2max(b), R²)). For u_vec in b: u_0 = sqrt(1 − |u_vec|²) ≥ s_b, so
Re(λ_i u) = λ_{i,0} u_0 − λ_{i,vec}·u_vec ≥ 1 − η²/2, i.e. |λ_i u − 1|² = 2 − 2 Re(λ_i u) ≤ η². ∎
